config.title: useImperativeHandle

intro.title: useImperativeHandle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses a template reference variable to access child component methods, mimicking the 'useImperativeHandle' pattern from React. You'll learn how to expose specific methods from a child component to its parent, allowing controlled interaction. The core concept involves using Angular's @ViewChild decorator and TypeScript to define a public API for a component. You'll work with component templates, class methods, and event binding to achieve this functionality.
intro.usecase: In real-world Angular applications, developers often need to expose specific component methods to parent components while keeping internal implementation details private. This pattern is crucial when building complex form controls, custom input components, or interactive widgets where parent components need to programmatically trigger actions like validation, focus management, or data submission. For example, in a dashboard with multiple data visualization components, a parent dashboard controller might need to call `refreshData()` or `exportChart()` methods on child chart components without accessing their entire internal state. Similarly, in form-heavy applications like admin panels or CRUD interfaces, parent forms frequently need to invoke `validate()` or `reset()` on custom form field components to coordinate validation and submission across the entire form.

objectives: Implement a child component that exposes custom methods using forwardRef and useImperativeHandle
Configure a parent component to access the child's imperative methods via a template reference
Initialize and manipulate component state that triggers imperative child behaviors
Construct a TypeScript interface defining the exposed imperative handle contract
Bind UI events in the parent component to execute child component methods imperatively
Control child component functionality from the parent without relying on props or events
Integrate useImperativeHandle with Angular's lifecycle hooks for proper initialization
